skill.description: Design server-side conversion tracking for Facebook, TikTok, Google Ads, and Microsoft Advertising. Preserve click identifiers, deduplicate events, and verify purchase reporting.

skill.author: autonnel

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown syntax and conversion-tracking terminology, not executable code or system reconnaissance. The skill does recommend running Docker Compose from a remote repository and describes collecting and transmitting privacy-sensitive customer data.

remediation.issue: The setup directs users to run a remote repository through Docker Compose without an immutable commit or image digest.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the repository commit and container image digests, then require review of the Compose file before starting containers.

remediation.issue: The workflow handles IP addresses, user agents, click identifiers, and hashed customer identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent, retention, access-control, secret-storage, and data-deletion requirements for each supported platform and region.

content.value_statement: Browser restrictions and cross-domain funnels cause advertising platforms to miss purchases. This skill designs a durable capture, reporting, deduplication, and verification workflow.
actual_capabilities: Maps the seven stages from click identifier capture through conversion reconciliation.
Identifies required click parameters for Facebook, TikTok, Google Ads, and Microsoft Advertising.
Explains server-side persistence and cross-domain transfer of campaign identifiers.
Defines conversion event fields, customer identifier normalization, queueing, retries, and deduplication.
Provides checks for event delivery, match quality, order reconciliation, and click identifier coverage.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not production-ready integration code.
It does not replace legal review, consent management, or regional privacy compliance.
It does not guarantee agreement between platform attribution reports and order records.
Platform credentials, account configuration, API changes, and hosted-platform restrictions require separate validation.

use_cases.title: Repair Under-Reported Purchases
use_cases.description: Trace where campaign identifiers or purchase events disappear, then define fixes and measurable verification checks.

use_cases.title: Design a New Tracking Pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan capture, persistence, order attachment, queued delivery, and deduplication before paid traffic begins.

use_cases.title: Reconcile Platform Reporting
use_cases.description: Compare advertising conversions with order records while accounting for attribution windows and different reporting dates.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Tracking Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current funnel for server-side conversion tracking. Platforms: [platforms]. Funnel steps: [steps]. Domains: [domains]. Identify missing stages and priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing funnel

prompt_templates.title: Plan Click Identifier Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design click identifier and UTM capture for [funnel]. Explain server-side persistence, cross-domain transfer, order storage, and failure checks.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Conversion Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a platform-by-platform delivery specification for [platforms]. Include event fields, identifier normalization, credential needs, queue retries, and browser-server deduplication.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Reporting Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this reporting gap using [order totals], [platform totals], [click identifier coverage], and [debugger results]. Separate tracking loss from attribution differences.

output_examples.input: Facebook reports 62 purchases, while the order database records 100. Only 48 paid orders contain fbclid.
output: Primary finding: click identifier loss likely occurs before the order record.
Inspect landing capture, redirects, session persistence, and cross-domain checkout transfer.
Track daily click identifier coverage and compare it with the paid traffic share.

output_examples.input: A browser pixel and server event both report each purchase, but totals nearly doubled after launch.
output: Primary finding: browser and server events probably use different event identifiers.
Generate one stable purchase event identifier and send it through both delivery paths.
Confirm deduplication in the platform debugger before scaling traffic.

output_examples.input: Plan server-side purchase reporting for Facebook, TikTok, Google Ads, and Microsoft Advertising.
output: Capture each platform click identifier and campaign parameters on the first landing request.
Persist identifiers server-side, carry them across domains, and attach them to the order.
Queue platform deliveries with normalized customer identifiers, retries, deduplication, and reconciliation checks.

best_practices: Capture campaign identifiers before redirects and persist them in a first-party server session.
Use one stable purchase event identifier for browser and server events.
Verify delivery, match quality, click identifier coverage, and order reconciliation after every tracking change.
anti_patterns: Do not add only a server event while ignoring identifier capture and order attachment.
Do not send conversion requests inline with payment or checkout processing.
Do not treat hashed customer data as anonymous or bypass consent requirements.

faq.question: Does server-side tracking recover every missing conversion?
faq.answer: No. It improves delivery and matching, but consent restrictions, missing identifiers, and attribution rules still affect reported totals.

faq.question: Why must click identifiers be stored on the order?
faq.answer: Order storage survives session loss, supports retries and backfills, and enables reliable joins between purchases and advertising clicks.

faq.question: How are duplicate browser and server events prevented?
faq.answer: Both paths must send the same stable event identifier for each purchase. Platform debuggers should confirm successful deduplication.

faq.question: Should platform totals equal database orders?
faq.answer: No. Attribution windows, view-through credit, click dates, and platform-specific rules create expected differences.

faq.question: Is hashed customer information still personal data?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply consent, access, retention, deletion, and regional privacy requirements before collecting or transmitting it.

faq.question: Can this skill configure every advertising account automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and verification guidance. Credentials, account permissions, platform settings, and current API requirements need direct validation.
